r1-handoff.imperative: Did the change do what the handoff asked, within its allowed scope? Record pass/fail with a finding.
r1-handoff.finding: Checks (a)-(f) verified by DRIVING, not reading. (b) R2 TOTAL: 482 real session ids harvested from 5496 JSON files + journals -> 0 failures, 0 key collisions, 111 slash-bearing, literal $SID/$SESSION/'impl-300-g3-$(date' all normalize; None/blank -> unowned gauge.json (absence of owner, not rejection); skip/uncalibrated structurally unreachable (every key ends -<12hex>). (c) R3 BOTH halves against the real engine: leaseless reads unowned gauge.json and trips at 93% hard exactly as today; leased with no owner-keyed file returns None with a shared 0.93 gauge.json sitting right there unread (no fallback); owner-keyed file is read when present. (d) AMENDED per RULING-2: #488 exact shape WRITES, and same-owner-ness is LOAD-BEARING (identical scenario with only the owner strings differing SKIPS) so it pins the same-owner path specifically, not merely two candidates; skip stays VISIBLE - drove the two-owner case and saw gauge-skip.json with reason=ambiguous-binding candidate_count=2 in BOTH dirs. Also drove R4 row 2 (2 distinct dirs, one owner): both candidates written. (e) #601 present and FIRES on owner-keyed files: reading sampled 30m before claimed_at is declined (SILENT advisory, no trip); same file sampled after claimed_at trips at 95%. (f) owner_key/gauge_filename defined ONCE in scripts/gauge_reader.py; hook and engine both delegate, no reimplementation. OBSERVATION (a): the result's blanket claim 'Nothing refuses where it previously permitted' is imprecise. Enumerated the only two refusal consumers (start begin-work guard ~:2073 and advance's require_why at :3419, both gated on _trip_hard_band_reading, both byte-unchanged). Two paths CAN now refuse where they previously permitted: (i) R1 - a leased agent now reads its OWN reading instead of whichever agent wrote last, so a genuine over-hard fill refuses where a foreign low reading used to permit; (ii) R4/#488 - the same-owner multi-candidate case now writes where the count-based skip produced silence, and a restored reading can trip. Both are the ruled-on PURPOSE of the change, not side effects, and neither is a new CLASS of refusal. No new refusal requiring a float.

r4-quality.title: Quality vs inherited rules
r4-quality.imperative: Does the change meet the inherited project/section rules (the handoff's constraints)? Append a check per rule. Record pass/fail with a finding.
r4-quality.finding: CONSTRAINTS HONOURED: __pycache__ cleared before every measurement I took (#597); Linux + py 3.12; local Linux treated as the only real signal; #601's timestamp comparison present and firing, and R1's limit correctly STATED not overclaimed - both the result and the commit message say identity-not-time is NOT completed. Fresh-process rule honoured where it decides anything: I validated the installed by-path loader in a fresh process with CLAUDE_PROJECT_DIR UNSET, and it resolves via __file__ rather than the env var, so the claim does not rest on injection. test_gauge_chain_writer_to_trip.py does pin CLAUDE_PROJECT_DIR in its subprocess env, but as a documented and separately-asserted CONTAINMENT fence (#271: an unfenced subprocess resolves project dir to the developer's real checkout), not as proof of harness delivery. _owner_mismatch drives correctly: a 0.97 over-hard record stamped for a foreign owner is DECLINED with a loud CONTEXT GAUGE DECLINED advisory and does not trip - quiet direction, never a new refusal. FAIL REASON - UNTESTED GOVERNOR BRANCH (R4 row 2). '2+ DISTINCT candidates all under ONE owner -> write every candidate' is implemented and I confirmed it works by driving it (two work dirs, one binding key, one engine_session -> both owner-keyed files written, no sidecars). But NOTHING TESTS IT. Mutation proof: replacing 'unattributable = len(targets) > 1 and (None in owners or len(owners) > 1)' with 'unattributable = len(targets) > 1' - i.e. reverting row 2 to the old skip-on-count - leaves ALL 616 gauge tests GREEN (mutation asserted applied, then restored byte-identical, git diff clean). Every existing multi-candidate test uses two DIFFERENT owners (eng-1/eng-2) and so exercises the skip branch; the #488 test covers the same-DIRECTORY case, which dedupes to ONE candidate and never enters the multi-candidate write loop. This is the exact silent-regression shape this subsystem has been burned by three times (#252, #271, #488): a future simplification back to a count check would restore the #488-class dark governor for the multi-directory same-owner case with no failing test anywhere. NOTE for the record: ADMIRAL_RULING-2 point 1 states #488's case 'lands in row 2 - write every candidate'. It does not; same dir + same owner dedupes to a single candidate (row 1). The OUTCOME the Admiral required - it still writes - holds, and the required test is present and same-owner-discriminating, so the ruling is satisfied; only its row attribution is off by one row.

r6-fowler.title: Refactoring pass (Fowler code smells)
r6-fowler.imperative: Run the refactoring / code-smell pass (SKILL.md 'Refactoring pass'). Render a verdict on each Fowler baseline smell (long method, large class, duplicated code, feature envy, data clumps, primitive obsession, long parameter list, shotgun surgery, divergent change, message chains, speculative generality, comments-as-deodorant): flagged / overridden / absent. Smells are judgment calls, ALWAYS subordinate to the repo's documented standards — an override needs a logged standard + reason. Record the pass to .agent-work/cleanup-b-context-identity/FOWLER_PASS.json (from templates/FOWLER_PASS.template.json), run scripts/verify_fowler_pass.py .agent-work/cleanup-b-context-identity/FOWLER_PASS.json (it refuses a skipped smell or an unlogged override), then record pass/fail with a finding. This item's postcondition command resolves the record path from cleanup-b-context-identity alone -- the same substitution you already make everywhere else in this survey (line 2) -- so no separate placeholder to fill and no way to leave it stale. REPAIR PATH -- only if the record path ever needs to move off that fixed convention, correct it through the engine with `amend --delta <file>` whose single op is `retext-check` on this item's c1, never by hand-editing this survey. There, --authority is the dispatching Commander named in your reviewer handoff (never a string you invent), and --reason is why the path changed. Do NOT silently skip this item.

FLAGGED, all observations not blockers: (1) handle_post_tool_use is 175 lines / 91 non-comment and this change grew it - extracting the attribution decision would also give R4 row 2 the unit-test seam it currently lacks, tying this smell directly to the r4-quality finding; (2) the unowned name is hardcoded three times (gauge_writer_hook.py:205,:209, checklist_engine.py:1420) beside its declared single definition gauge_reader.GAUGE_FILENAME - the same drift hazard the design note argues against, but self-limiting since those literals are only reachable when the reader failed to load, where no owner-keyed read happens either; (3) the (gauge_path, owner) 2-tuple is threaded through five sites and discarded as _owner in three, earning a NamedTuple in a file that already uses a frozen dataclass. OVERRIDDEN with logged standard + reason: primitive-obsession (the owner crosses a process boundary as a filename and JSON field; gauge_reader's portability contract forbids the import and R2 requires a TOTAL normalizer, not a constructor that could reject); shotgun-surgery (the ripple is inherent to a cross-process FILE FORMAT, and the repo's own SCRIPT_RUNTIME_COMPANIONS is the documented mechanism for the coupling - which this change uses); divergent-change (ADMIRAL_RULING-1 governs checklist_engine.py by explicit REGION fence rather than by splitting, and splitting would itself breach that fence; regions verified respected by AST extraction); comments-as-deodorant (global-crew.md 'Agent-facing. Dense by design.'; the comments carry decision provenance that lives nowhere else while the map is DEGRADED, and the code beneath them is short and plainly named). SPECULATIVE-GENERALITY checked specifically rather than waved past: resolve_gauge_path is kept alongside resolve_gauge_targets but retains real current callers and tests, so it is a compatibility view, not an unused seam.

consolidation.summary: APPROVE. #600 does what R1-R4 (as amended by ADMIRAL_RULING-2) require, verified by driving every claim rather than reading it. R2 is TOTAL over 482 real session ids with 0 failures and 0 key collisions; R3 holds on both halves against the real engine; R4-as-amended holds with #488's case writing, same-owner-ness load-bearing, and the skip visibly sidecar'd; #601's timestamp guard is present and fires on owner-keyed files; the claim path is byte-identical by AST extraction; no fenced file is touched. RED (16 failed/1 passed) and GREEN (4 passed) both reproduced independently, the before/after demo reproduces in both directions with a byte-identical script, blast radius reproduces exactly at 23 files/186 occurrences, and the failure-set difference against a re-measured main baseline is ZERO (branch 3104 passed/6 skipped/0 failed vs main 3089 passed/7 skipped/0 failed). All three departures adjudicated: 1 resolved by the Admiral, 2 CONFIRMED JUSTIFIED by installing and driving the loader, 3 CONFIRMED with a bounded advisory-only residual. One fail carried: R4 row 2 is implemented and works but is untested (mutation-proved). Three triage candidates flagged.
consolidation.override_reason: r4-quality is recorded fail for a real finding that does not bar this change: R4 row 2 (2+ distinct candidates under one owner -> write every candidate) has no test, mutation-proved by reverting it to skip-on-count and watching all 616 gauge tests stay green. It is a TEST-COVERAGE gap, not a correctness defect - I drove the branch directly and it behaves exactly as R4 requires. The Admiral's literally required test (R4: pin #488's exact shape and assert the write happens) IS present and I verified it is same-owner-discriminating, so the ruling's own acceptance criterion is met; row 2 is an ADDITIONAL branch I found uncovered. Blocking would cost a rework cycle on a lane that has already ended at a context boundary twice, for a change whose behaviour is verified correct and whose suite is green with a zero failure-set difference. Recording it as a fail rather than softening it to a pass keeps the finding intact, and it is filed as triage candidate tc1 for g1-integrate.

triage_candidates.statement: Pin R4 row 2 with a test: one binding key, one engine_session, two DISTINCT work directories -> BOTH owner-keyed gauge files written. Today reverting that branch to skip-on-count leaves all 616 gauge tests green (reviewer-verified by mutation), so the #488-class dark-governor regression could return unnoticed for the multi-directory same-owner case.

Sidecars are per-directory and unowned while readings are per-owner, so one owner's gauge-skip.json / gauge-uncalibrated.json advisory can be rendered to a different owner sharing the work directory. Reviewer-verified as advisory-only: gauge_reader.read() on a sidecar returns None, so it can never become a Reading and can never cause a trip or refusal. Bounded residual, widened slightly by #600.

A SessionStart/stop hook told this reviewer crew to drive its PARENT Commander's execute gate, because it resolves SPINE_FILE from the inherited environment (SPINE_SESSION named constellation/cleanup-b-context-identity/execute/commander). Same defect class as #600 one layer up: ambient inherited context deciding 'which run am I in'. Acting on it would have required a --force takeover of a live parent's lease and deadlocked the wave. Second occurrence - the g1 implementer reported it too.
